messages.subject: xgboost
parts:
hello, i'm new to the group and very excited about Renjin!

i see that the current build for xgboost has an error, but is there a way to use older versions, or is it the case that xgboost hasn't ever worked in Renjin?  If so, I would love to advocate for it's development, as it's a very popular ML tool.

messages.author: 3b104dc6686d0c85
messages.subject: Re: xgboost
parts:
Hi David,

glad to hear that you're excited about Renjin!

It looks like xgboost has never been successfully compiled for Renjin. This is partly due to the package's internal C++ code which our transpiler isn't yet able to convert to Java bytecode, but also due to the unavailability of its dependencies. Unfortunately, these aren't minor dependencies either as data.table, for example, uses GNU R's C API in very "creative" ways and thus will be a challenge to compile for Renjin. But this is not to say that it's impossible to get xgboost to work in Renjin.

If you are of the inpatient type, a quicker option could be to wrap a pure-Java implementation in an R package for Renjin. Our documentation includes pointers on how to create extension packages here: http://docs.renjin.org/en/latest/writing-renjin-extensions.html and we have a few example package on GitHub such as rjson and xml2 (in various stages of completeness).

Creating these kinds of packages or working on improving Renjin's compatibility with specific CRAN packages are part of our commercial offerings so get in touch with us if you are interested in getting our help.

Maarten
